out.reasoning: Starting from the market’s 0.655, I modestly raise the probability of a July hold. June’s unanimous decision and broad support for maintaining rates indicate policy inertia (E1, E3). Warsh’s July 14 emphasis on persistent inflation and a broadly stable labor market suggests little urgency to cut (E6). Elevated core PCE inflation also discourages immediate easing (E4). Meanwhile, June’s energy-driven CPI decline reduces the immediate case for a hike without establishing sustained underlying disinflation (E5). Weak payroll growth creates some easing risk (E2), while hawkish participants leave a hike possible. With only two weeks until the meeting, these competing pressures favor another hold, but justify only a modest departure from the informed market estimate.

I modestly raise the market’s 0.655 estimate to 0.70. Weak payroll growth creates some case for a cut, while elevated inflation leaves a hike possible. With only two weeks until the meeting, these conflicting signals make holding the upper bound at 3.75% the likeliest decision.

I modestly raise the market’s 0.655 estimate. June’s unanimous hold and the chair’s July 14 description of a broadly stable labor market favor continued patience.
